title: Nanoimprint-only array layers, DUV periphery: EUV-free 1T1C DRAM
idea: Box: Si-capacitor charge x buried-channel access x voltage sense amp x 2D monolithic x 300 mm Si x jet-and-flash nanoimprint. The strictly periodic array layers (active, buried WL, BL, storage-node contact, capacitor holes) are imprinted from e-beam-written masters into jetted resist, while the irregular, relaxed-pitch periphery stays on DUV immersion; overlay is held by a magnification-actuated template chuck and in-situ moire alignment marks.
why: Litho-bound capital (fact 4): replaces 5-7 EUV layers with imprint tools at roughly 1/4-1/5 of EUV capex and ~90% less litho energy; claims 20-30% lower wafer cost if imprint defectivity reaches <0.1/cm2.

title: Line-only crossbar 1S1C DRAM: OTS selector plus capacitor, SAOP-patterned
idea: Box: MIM charge x ovonic threshold switch (two-terminal) x current-pulse sensing x stackable crossbar decks x Si x self-aligned octuple patterning of lines only. Each cell is a vertical OTS in series with a small capacitor at a WL/BL crossing, so a deck is just two orthogonal line/space layers from DUV+SAOP etched into self-aligned pillars; the OTS snaps on above Vth to charge/read and its off-state holds the charge.
why: Removes hole and contact layers, the ones that force EUV (fact 4); 4F2 with two masks per deck and decks stack like cross-point so density grows without litho; risk is OTS sub-threshold leakage and threshold drift capping retention.

title: Thickness-defined vertical IGZO 3D DRAM on Gen-8.5 display glass
idea: Box: oxide gain-cell node charge x vertical IGZO TFT whose channel length is a deposited film thickness x current sensing x 48-tier monolithic stack x Gen-8.5 glass panel x i-line display lithography plus ALD. Every critical dimension (gate length, dielectric, node) comes from film thickness or recess time rather than resolution, so 1.5 um display steppers suffice and bits/area come from tier count on a 5.5 m2 substrate (~75x a 300 mm wafer).
why: Capital intensity and U.S. manufacturability: borrows the display-fab cost model ($/m2 processed ~10-30x below DRAM fabs); claims 5-10x lower capex per bit for a capacity tier; risk is panel-scale ALD uniformity and per-tier density.

title: Crucible-free kerfless DRAM substrates via porous-silicon epitaxial lift-off
idea: Box: any cell x any access x any sense x 2D monolithic x epitaxial Si foil on a reusable seed x CVD epitaxy. One CZ seed wafer is anodized into double-layer porous Si and sealed by H2 anneal; a 50-100 um device-grade epi layer is grown, bonded to a recycled-Si or glass carrier and lifted off, and the seed is reused 20-50 times.
why: Scarce resources: cuts Spruce Pine high-purity-quartz crucible use and CZ pulling per wafer by ~20-50x and eliminates slicing kerf; substrate is ~5-10% of DRAM wafer cost.

title: Atmospheric spatial-ALD tools for capacitor high-k without vacuum chambers
idea: Box: ZrO2/Al2O3/ZrO2 capacitor charge x standard access x standard sensing x 2D x 300 mm Si x spatial ALD. Wafers rotate under gas-bearing heads with separated precursor and oxidant zones at atmospheric pressure, so growth rate is decoupled from purge time; pressure-pulsed dwell zones let precursor diffuse to the bottom of 70:1 holes before the wafer moves on.
why: Throughput and tool capex for the capacitor module: 5-10x wafers/hour per tool vs temporal ALD and no vacuum hardware, saving hundreds of millions per 100k-wafer fab; risk is step coverage at AR 70.

title: Hydrogen-backside electrostatic chucks free etch and deposition from helium
idea: Box: unchanged cell x fab-method axis set to backside thermal gas. Replace helium backside cooling on electrostatic chucks (capacitor cryo-etch, CVD, ALD) with low-pressure H2 or forming gas, whose thermal conductivity (~0.18 W/m-K) matches helium, inside a closed recirculating plenum with on-site electrolytic H2, catalytic recombiner and leak sensors.
why: Helium chokepoint (Qatar ~30% offline): backside cooling and leak check are the main fab helium uses; removing them de-risks wafer output; risk is safety qualification and edge-plasma interaction.

title: Bottom-up VLS-grown vertical nanowire access transistors on landing pads
idea: Box: Si capacitor charge x vertical gate-all-around Si nanowire grown, not etched x voltage sense amp x capacitor-over-transistor x Si x vapor-liquid-solid growth from Al or Sn catalyst dots placed by electroless self-aligned deposition on bitline contacts. ALD then wraps the gate and a spacer etch forms wordlines, giving a 4F2 vertical cell without an EUV pillar exposure.
why: Litho capital (fact 4) and density: removes 1-2 EUV layers and the pillar etch while enabling 4F2 (~33% smaller than 6F2); risk is catalyst contamination, growth-direction yield and diameter uniformity.

title: Area-selective deposition grows capacitor electrodes up from landing pads
idea: Box: TiN/ZrO2 capacitor charge x standard BCAT x voltage sense amp x 2D x Si x area-selective CVD with inhibitor monolayers. Instead of depositing a 1.5 um mold, etching 70:1 holes and stripping the mold, Ru or TiN pillars grow upward only on the landing pads while the dielectric is inhibitor-passivated, then high-k and top electrode fill around them.
why: Eliminates the highest-AR etch, mold strip and anti-leaning support layers (~8-12 steps and the cryo-etch fleet); claims ~10% wafer cost; risk is selectivity loss over 1 um of growth and lateral mushrooming bridging cells.

title: Thin-tunnel charge-trap 3D NOR DRAM built in idle NAND fabs
idea: Box: nitride-trapped charge behind a 1.5-2 nm tunnel oxide x vertical poly-Si channel in parallel NOR strings x current sensing x 200+ word-plane stack x Si x existing 3D NAND toolset. The thin tunnel oxide trades retention (seconds) for 10-50 ns writes, refreshed like DRAM, while NOR wiring gives random access; staircase, channel-hole and replacement-gate modules are reused unchanged.
why: Capital and time: converts already-depreciated NAND capacity into DRAM-class capacity without a new $15B fab, density from tiers not litho; risk is trap endurance (~1e10) vs DRAM's unlimited, requiring a DRAM cache in front.

title: Edge-printed sidewall interconnects replace TSVs in HBM stacks
idea: Box: standard DRAM die x standard access x standard sensing x die stack wired on its edge x thinned Si x aerosol-jet plus laser-sintered metallization on the polished stack face. Pads routed to die edges are exposed on one face of the stack and 5-10 um pitch vertical lines are printed down that face, with capacitive face-to-face coupling carrying the fastest lanes.
why: HBM TSV tax (fact 6): removes TSV etch, fill, reveal and keep-out zones that drive ~3x area per bit and 20-30% yield loss; claims 20-40% HBM area back; risk is edge I/O density and signal integrity.

title: Mux-in-array, sense-out-of-array: oxide-mux array die bonded at micron pitch
idea: Box: Si capacitor charge x BCAT x sense amps moved to a separate logic die x wafer-to-wafer hybrid bond at 1 um pitch x Si x array die fabbed with array plus BEOL IGZO 1:32 bitline multiplexers only. Because bonding cannot reach 30 nm bitline pitch, each bond pad serves 32 bitlines through an oxide-transistor mux, while sense amps, decoders and I/O come from a cheap mature-node logic wafer.
why: Periphery takes ~49% of the die (fact 7): array wafer sheds ~15-20 periphery masks and each DRAM-fab wafer carries ~1.6-1.9x more bits; risk is mux charge-sharing eroding sense margin.

title: Fluidic self-assembly of known-good DRAM micro-tiles onto wafer carriers
idea: Box: standard cell x standard access x standard sensing x micro-tile assembly x 300 mm passive-RDL carrier x shape-keyed fluidic self-assembly. Tested 1-4 mm2 DRAM tiles (yield ~99% because tiny) are suspended in liquid and settle into keyed recesses on a carrier with fine-pitch RDL, building large memories with near-100% assembled yield and no pick-and-place.
why: Yield and capital: small-tile yield replaces big-die yield loss so a cheaper, EUV-free, higher-defect process becomes economic; ~1e6 tiles/hour vs ~1e4 for pick-and-place; risk is inter-tile interconnect density.

title: Minienvironment-only DRAM fab with defect-tolerant wafer-scale sparing
idea: Box: standard cell x standard access x self-testing sense with built-in repair x wafer-scale integration x Si x sealed-FOUP and tool-minienvironment fab in an ISO-6 shell. Arrays carry 10-15% spare subarrays and on-die BIST remaps defective rows at power-up, so the higher particle density of a cheap building is absorbed by architecture rather than by an ISO-1 ballroom.
why: Capital intensity: the cleanroom building is ~20-30% of fab capex; an ISO-6 shell could halve it and cut 1-2 years of construction, at a cost of ~10% array area for spares.

title: Cell-stamp e-beam: a million shaped beamlets each write one cell
idea: Box: standard cell x standard access x standard sensing x 2D x Si x massively parallel e-beam with a programmable aperture plate shaped to the cell motif. Because the array is a lattice, each of ~1e6 beamlets is shaped into the same cell feature (parallel character projection) and the stage scan makes each beamlet write its own sub-array tile, so there are no masks and shot count falls by orders of magnitude vs pixel writing.
why: Mask cost and EUV dependence (fact 4); periodicity attacks e-beam's throughput problem; target 20-40 wafers/hour per column cluster at ~$30-50M; risk is beamlet uniformity and stitching.

title: Low-aspect-ratio capacitor from ALD rutile-TiO2/SrTiO3 on Ru, k~100
idea: Box: k 100-150 dielectric charge x standard access x standard sensing x 2D x Si x ALD on Ru/RuO2 electrodes that template rutile or perovskite growth below 450 C. With k~100 vs ~40 today, the same ~5 fF fits in an AR ~25 pillar, so the module drops the cryo-etch, the support mesh and two hardmask layers; leakage is held by Al doping and a thin wide-gap interface layer.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1) attacked through process: AR 70 to 25 removes the hardest etch and its helium-cooled tools, ~5-8% wafer cost; risk is leakage of narrow-gap high-k at ~0.4 nm EOT.

title: Electroless ruthenium wordlines and plugs escape tungsten and WF6
idea: Box: standard cell x buried-wordline access with Ru gate fill x standard sensing x 2D x Si x seedless electroless or ALD-seeded Ru plating. Buried wordlines and contact plugs, today CVD W from WF6, are filled bottom-up by barrier-free Ru (short electron mean free path keeps resistivity low in 10 nm trenches).
why: Tungsten chokepoint (China ~80%) and fluorine chemistry removed; barrier-free fill gives ~30% lower WL RC or allows a thinner WL that lowers GIDL; Ru needed is micrograms per die.

title: Universal array-tile consortium: one shared mask set across vendors
idea: Box: business axis set to shared mask and process. U.S. and allied fabs standardize a 1T1C array tile (cell pitch, sub-array size, BL/WL interface) whose ~20 array masks and process module are developed once and licensed per wafer, so new entrants and foundries only design periphery.
why: Capital and time to enter (U.S. ~1-2% share): removes ~$50-100M of mask and module development and ~2-3 years per entrant; risk is IP and competitive reluctance.

title: Public EUV utility leases scanners per exposed layer to DRAM makers
idea: Box: fab-method axis set to tool ownership. A government-chartered utility owns EUV scanners installed inside participating fabs and bills per exposed wafer-layer at a ~3% cost of capital instead of fab WACC ~10%, with take-or-pay terms moving depreciation risk off DRAM balance sheets during downturns.
why: Depreciation is ~55% of wafer cost (fact 4): cheaper capital on ~$200M tools cuts per-wafer litho cost ~30-40% and damps boom-bust capex swings; risk is political.

title: Three 60-degree line exposures intersect into honeycomb capacitor holes
idea: Box: Si capacitor charge x standard access x standard sensing x 2D x Si x triple sidewall-image-transfer at 0, 60 and 120 degrees. Three spacer line arrays are stacked as hardmasks and the etch opens only where all three gaps coincide, giving a hexagonal hole lattice at ~18 nm half-pitch from DUV line exposures, self-aligned to active lines set by the 0-degree array.
why: Removes the EUV or LELE hole layer for storage-node contact and capacitor (fact 4), since line/space is far easier than holes for DUV; ~1-2 EUV layers saved; risk is compounded LER and hexagonal hole CD uniformity.

title: Cold repeated ion-cut tier stacking with microwave dopant activation
idea: Box: gain-cell or capacitor charge x planar single-crystal Si transistor per tier x standard sensing x 8-16 tiers via layer transfer x Si x hydrogen ion-cut plus microwave anneal below 450 C. Each tier is a single-crystal film transferred from a reusable donor onto the previous patterned tier, exposed with the same DUV masks, and activated by microwaves that couple to dopants without cooking lower tiers.
why: 3D DRAM manufacturability (fact 2) with single-crystal channels and reused masks, so bits/area scale with tiers at flat mask count; risk is per-tier yield and reaching the ~26-tier break-even.

title: Backside capacitors: storage nodes etched into the thinned wafer back
idea: Box: deep-trench charge x vertical-channel access x standard sensing x front/back split x thinned Si on carrier x backside trench etch self-aligned to buried drains. After front-side transistors and bitlines, the wafer is bonded face-down and thinned, and capacitor trenches are etched from the back into bulk Si landing on each transistor's buried drain, so capacitors no longer compete with bitlines for front-side space.
why: Removes storage-node-contact and landing-pad layers (2-3 masks incl. ~1 EUV) and gives free capacitor height (Cs >8 fF); reuses backside-power tools now entering logic fabs.

title: Short segmented bitlines with local sense let 1.5 fF capacitors suffice
idea: Box: shallow capacitor charge (~1.5 fF) x standard access x hierarchical local sense amp every 32 cells placed under the array x 2D x Si x capacitor AR ~20. Cutting bitline length from 512-1024 cells to 32 lowers bitline capacitance ~20x, preserving the transfer ratio with a capacitor one third the size, so the capacitor module becomes a shallow single-etch step.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1) traded on the sensing axis: AR 70 to 20 removes the highest-capex module and cuts BL CV2 energy ~10x; extra sense amps hide under the array.

title: One-hole cell: capacitor and vertical oxide transistor share one hole
idea: Box: MIM charge at hole bottom x vertical IGZO channel lining the hole top x voltage sense amp x BEOL over periphery x Si x single etched hole with sequential ALD fill and recess. One hole receives bottom electrode and high-k, is recessed, then gets a lined IGZO channel and gate-all-around wordline fill, so storage-node contacts, landing pads and their overlay steps disappear.
why: Mask count and overlay (fact 4): removes 3-4 masks including EUV contacts, natively 4F2, and sits over periphery (fact 7); risk is IGZO quality on the hole sidewall and series resistance.

title: Self-ordered anodic alumina pores as 100:1 capacitor molds on chip
idea: Box: MIM charge x sputtered IGZO TFT x voltage sense amp x BEOL test chip x Si/SiO2 x two-step Al anodization in oxalic acid. A sputtered Al film is anodized into hexagonally ordered pores (~60-100 nm pitch, AR >100) with positions seeded by a light EBL pre-pattern, then ALD TiN/HfO2/TiN coats the pores, so the capacitor mold forms in a beaker, not a cryo-etcher.
why: Capacitor module capital (fact 1): a ~$2k anodization bath replaces a $5M+ high-AR etcher, with AR 100-500 possible (10-30 fF/cell); every step uses university sputter, EBL, ALD and wet benches.

title: Beaker-grown anodic Nb/Ta/Hf oxide as the capacitor dielectric
idea: Box: barrier-type anodic oxide charge x EBL-patterned IGZO access x standard sensing x 2D test array x Si x room-temperature electrochemical anodization of a sputtered valve metal. The bottom electrode's surface is anodized at ~1.5-2 nm/V into a dense dielectric (Nb2O5 k~40, Ta2O5 k~25) whose thickness is set by a voltage and whose pinholes self-heal during growth.
why: Removes the ALD tool from the dielectric step and self-heals defects for yield; buildable with a potentiostat and wet bench; risk is anodic-oxide leakage below 5 nm and contacting the electrode during anodization.

title: Metal-assisted chemical etching carves 100:1 capacitor trenches without plasma
idea: Box: Si trench charge x planar Si MOSFET access x standard sensing x 2D x Si x MacEtch with an EBL-patterned noble-metal mesh in HF/H2O2. The catalytic film sinks vertically into Si at room temperature, carving smooth high-AR holes in a wet bench; the catalyst is stripped and holes are lined by ALD.
why: Highest-AR etch with no plasma tool or helium-cooled chuck (AR >100 shown in research); capex <$10k; risk is catalyst contamination in a DRAM-grade flow and verticality below 50 nm.

title: Spin-coated, UV-cured indium-zinc oxide access transistors in BEOL
idea: Box: MIM charge x solution-processed InZnO TFT x voltage sense amp x BEOL x Si or glass x sol-gel spin coating plus deep-UV photo-annealing below 250 C. A nitrate precursor coats the topography and 185/254 nm UV generates ozone and radicals that condense the oxide network, reaching 5-20 cm2/Vs with no vacuum deposition.
why: Removes sputter/ALD clusters from the access-device module (capital); uses only a spin coater and UV lamp; risk is trap density widening the leakage tail and thickness control in 3D topography.

title: Double-angle shadow evaporation sets 20 nm channels without fine lithography
idea: Box: oxide-node charge x lateral oxide TFT whose source-drain gap is set by evaporation angle x current sensing x 2D x glass or Si x Dolan resist bridge plus two tilted e-beam evaporations, borrowed from superconducting-qubit junction fab. The gap equals bridge height times the tangent difference of the two angles, so a ~200 nm optical feature yields a ~20 nm self-aligned channel.
why: Sidesteps litho-bound scaling (fact 4): the critical dimension comes from angle and film thickness, not resolution; any university evaporator with a tilt stage works; risk is wafer-scale angle uniformity.

title: Nanosphere monolayer defines both access pillars and capacitor posts
idea: Box: MIM charge x vertical Si pillar GAA x voltage sense amp x capacitor-over-pillar x Si x Langmuir-Blodgett colloidal monolayer. A close-packed polystyrene sphere layer is O2-plasma shrunk and used to etch hexagonal pillars; after gate ALD and planarization, the exposed pillar tops seed self-aligned capacitor posts, so one self-assembled layer sets the whole lattice with zero overlay.
why: Mask-free cell lattice at 100-200 nm pitch (smaller with smaller spheres) using a trough and RIE; shows an EUV-free hexagonal array path; risk is domain boundaries, mapped out as defect rows by BIST.

title: Lloyd's-mirror crossed interference exposures print maskless pillar lattices
idea: Box: Si charge x vertical pillar transistor x standard sensing x 2D x Si x 266/325 nm laser Lloyd's-mirror interference lithography, two exposures at 90 degrees. Interference fringes print a perfectly periodic dot lattice over the wafer in seconds with no mask, and array-edge cuts plus periphery are added with a contact-aligner exposure.
why: Mask and EUV dependence for periodic arrays: a ~$50k optical table vs a $150M+ scanner; 100-150 nm pitch today, path below 40 nm with 193 nm immersion interference; risk is overlay of later layers to the lattice.

title: Glancing-angle-deposited nanohelix electrodes multiply capacitor area, maskless
idea: Box: MIM charge on a 3D nanocolumn electrode x standard access x standard sensing x 2D x Si x glancing-angle e-beam evaporation at ~85 degrees with substrate rotation. Self-shadowing grows isolated TiN or Ru columns or helices of set height on EBL-seeded storage pads, then ALD dielectric and top electrode coat them for 5-20x area with no high-AR etch.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1) by additive self-shadowing instead of etching; needs only an evaporator with a motorized stage; risk is column porosity raising leakage and fill conformality.

title: Reusable silicon-nitride nanostencils pattern memory layers resist-free
idea: Box: MIM charge x evaporated oxide TFT x standard sensing x 2D x any substrate x deposition through EBL+DRIE-made SiN membrane stencils. Metals, oxides and semiconductors are evaporated through aligned membrane apertures, skipping resist, develop, etch and strip, and the stencil is cleaned and reused hundreds of times.
why: Process steps and chemicals: 4-5 steps per layer collapse to one, suited to low-capex BEOL memory layers; risk is aperture clogging and edge blur below ~50 nm.

title: Block-copolymer holes hardened by sequential infiltration for deep etch
idea: Box: Si trench charge x planar access x standard sensing x 2D x Si x PS-b-PMMA cylinder graphoepitaxy in EBL-written guides, ALD sequential infiltration (TMA/H2O) turning PMMA into an AlOx hardmask, then cryo-DRIE. This yields 20-30 nm holes at ~40 nm pitch with a self-made inorganic mask robust enough for AR >30 silicon etch.
why: EUV-free sub-40 nm hole arrays (fact 4) from a spin coater, ALD and ICP; risk is DSA defectivity (needs ~1/cm2) and placement error.

title: Planar sol-gel BST capacitor, flash-lamp crystallized, ends deep etching
idea: Box: paraelectric (Ba,Sr)TiO3 charge (k~300) x standard access x standard sensing x 2D x Si x spin-on sol-gel plus millisecond xenon flash-lamp anneal. The flash crystallizes only the top ~100 nm into perovskite while the substrate stays below 400 C, so a near-planar 1:1 to 3:1 capacitor on Pt or SrRuO3 reaches ~5 fF.
why: Removes high-AR capacitor modules entirely (fact 1) with a spin coater and flash/RTP tool; risk is grain-boundary leakage and dead-layer k collapse in films under 20 nm.

title: 77-kelvin DRAM: crude poly-Si transistors hold charge for hours
idea: Box: MIM charge x solid-phase-crystallized poly-Si TFT (leaky at 300 K) x voltage sense amp x 2D x glass or Si x PECVD a-Si plus furnace crystallization. At 77 K off-current falls by >1e6, so grain-boundary-limited TFTs from a low-mask university flow meet retention for liquid-nitrogen-cooled racks.
why: Uses temperature to relax process quality (no single-crystal Si, no EUV-grade junctions) and nearly removes refresh; LN2 cooling overhead is a few W per W; risk is system-level cryo adoption.

title: Nanoelectromechanical relay access device with true zero off-leakage
idea: Box: MIM charge x vertical NEMS contact relay (TiN beam over an ALD sacrificial gap) x voltage sense amp x BEOL x Si x three-mask surface micromachining plus vapor-HF release. An open relay passes no current, so the leakage tail (fact 3) and refresh vanish, and the device needs only sputter, ALD and release tools.
why: Kills refresh's 16-33% idle power and 10-20% bandwidth loss with crude lithography; risk is contact endurance (need >1e15 cycles, best ~1e10-1e12) and ns switching needing sub-100 nm beams.

title: Asymmetric-pitch pillars let conformal gates self-merge into wordlines
idea: Box: MIM charge x vertical GAA pillar x voltage sense amp x 2D x Si x one dot mask with pitch_x below twice the gate thickness and pitch_y above it. Conformal ALD TiN merges between pillars along x into continuous wordlines but stays split along y, and an anisotropic spacer etch isolates rows, giving wordlines with no wordline mask and ~3 masks for the cell.
why: Mask count and overlay (fact 4) with a 4F2-like vertical cell from ALD and RIE; risk is wordline resistance of thin merged TiN and pillar CD variation.

title: Direct nanoimprint of sol-gel high-k: pattern the dielectric itself
idea: Box: imprinted metal-oxide charge x standard access x standard sensing x 2D x Si x thermal imprint of a ZrO2/HfO2 sol-gel with a PDMS replica of an EBL master. The functional film acts as the resist: imprinting forms corrugated 3D capacitor shapes and a cure converts it to oxide, deleting the resist-etch-strip sequence.
why: Collapses ~4 steps per layer and avoids high-AR plasma etch for capacitor area enhancement using a university imprint press; risk is shrinkage cracking and leakage of solution-derived oxide.

title: Strain-driven self-rolling nanomembranes form Swiss-roll capacitors per cell
idea: Box: multi-turn rolled MIM charge x planar oxide TFT x standard sensing x vertical tube x Si x stress-engineered PECVD SiNx bilayer on a sacrificial Ge layer. A flat stack (strained bilayer, metal, ALD oxide, metal) is patterned with contact litho and released, and built-in strain rolls it into a 3-5 turn tube that multiplies capacitor area 10-50x per footprint with no high-AR etch.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1) solved by planar processing using PECVD, ALD and XeF2; risk is shrinking roll diameter below 200 nm (needs sub-10 nm films) and roll placement.

title: National nanofab DRAM shuttle with an open cell PDK
idea: Box: business/policy axis set to distributed prototyping. Fund an NNCI-style shuttle where a standardized 150 mm open DRAM cell flow (contact litho, EBL, ALD, sputter only) runs quarterly in ten university nanofabs with shared test chips, open PDK and characterization, so startups test new cells for ~$50k in months instead of $5-10M.
why: U.S. manufacturability and time-to-innovation: widens the funnel of new cell concepts using fabs that already exist; risk is translation from 150 mm university flows to 300 mm production.

title: Copy-exact university-toolset microfabs for low-capex capacity DRAM
idea: Box: business axis set to fab model. Build 5k-wafer/month 150-200 mm microfabs that copy a university nanofab toolset (used ALD, sputter, contact and imprint aligners, ICP, anodization) and run only university-buildable flows (anodic-pore capacitors, oxide TFTs, interference litho), sited by U.S. data centers to make CXL memory-expander tiers.
why: Capital: ~$50-100M per fab vs $15B and 1-2 years to build, diversifying supply; risk is the cost-per-bit gap to leading-edge DRAM (target within 2-3x for a capacity tier).

title: Bosch scallop-engineered corrugated capacitor walls double area
idea: Box: Si trench charge x standard access x standard sensing x 2D x Si x time-multiplexed DRIE with deliberately deep, tuned scallops. Etch/passivation cycle times are set to cut 30-50 nm periodic corrugations, then conformal ALD TiN/high-k/TiN coats them, giving a fixed-depth trench ~1.5-2.5x sidewall area from a recipe timing parameter.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1) at lower AR as a recipe-only change on any DRIE; risk is field crowding at corrugation tips raising leakage and scaling scallops below 50 nm holes.

title: Etch-free, lift-off-only 2T0C gain cell from evaporated ultrathin oxides
idea: Box: gate-node charge x ultrathin (3-4 nm) evaporated In2O3 write FET plus p-type SnO read FET x current sensing x 2D/BEOL x any substrate x additive lift-off only, no plasma etching. Every layer is evaporated or sputtered through patterned resist and lifted off, with an oxygen-plasma-free ozone anneal setting carrier density, so the flow needs an aligner, evaporator and sputterer only.
why: Process capital: removes etch tools and their gases from the flow while giving a complementary gain cell whose ultrathin channel keeps off-current low; risk is lift-off resolution and SnO stability.

title: Molecular-ruler multilayers define 10 nm gaps between electrodes
idea: Box: oxide-node charge x lateral nanogap TFT x current sensing x 2D x Si x molecular-ruler lithography. Alternating phosphonate/metal-ion layers self-assemble on a parent electrode to a thickness counted in molecules (~1.5 nm per layer), a second metal is deposited and lifted off, and dissolving the ruler leaves a precise gap for a channel or dielectric.
why: Critical dimension from self-assembly count, not litho resolution (fact 4), with beakers, an evaporator and a contact aligner; risk is wafer-scale uniformity and ruler defects.

title: Femtosecond-laser self-organized ripples write maskless wordline gratings
idea: Box: Si charge x lateral access x standard sensing x 2D x Si x laser-induced periodic surface structures. A scanned femtosecond laser on a thin hardmask film self-organizes ripples with period ~lambda/4 to lambda/2 (60-200 nm) through surface-plasmon interference, giving large-area line gratings transferred as wordline or bitline arrays without mask or resist.
why: Maskless periodic patterning with a ~$300k laser most university optics labs own; risk is period uniformity, bifurcation defects and alignment, most usable for self-aligned crossbar decks.

title: CVD-grown carbon-nanotube forests as high-area storage-node electrodes
idea: Box: MIM-on-CNT charge x planar access x standard sensing x 2D x Si x catalytic CVD of vertically aligned CNT bundles from lift-off-patterned Fe/Al2O3 dots on each storage pad. ALD Al2O3/HfO2 and TiN then wrap the forest, whose ~100x surface area per footprint gives fF-scale capacitance from small pads without etching holes.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1) by bottom-up growth with a tube furnace and ALD; risk is forest density on sub-100 nm pads, ~600 C growth temperature and ALD nucleation on CNT walls.
